clue.text: Idiot declines to give a good mark

parts.note: to decline is to drop or fall, so declines means dips
a teacher gives a tick for a correct answer

explanation.surface: A teacher grumbles that some fool refuses to award a high grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declines' reads as 'refuses', but here it means falls, DIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipstick is informal slang for a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Go in for some exercise information

parts.note: to go in for an activity is to do it
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Advice to sign up for a bit of exercise, presented as useful information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information or the lowdown on something.

clue.text: Valuable wine for Conservative head shows pomposity

indicators.note: one thing put in for another means it replaces it, so the wine takes the Conservative's place

parts.note: valuable means precious
tent is a deep red Spanish wine
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Swapping a Tory leader for expensive wine shows a pompous attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals a swap: the wine replaces the Conservative's letter. Tent is an old name for a dark Spanish red; 'head' is a headland, not a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a showy, self-important manner, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Chesty, having built house in windy arctic

indicators.note: the house is placed inside the rearranged letters
windy suggests blown about, so the letters of arctic are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cold-ridden explorer builds a hut in the blustery polar region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy' rearranges the letters of arctic into TRACIC, and 'in' places the house abbreviation within them after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoracic is the medical adjective for the thorax, the chest region.

clue.text: Press closely protecting English elite

indicators.note: the outer word protects by wrapping round the letter inside it

parts.note: to cram is to pack or press tightly

explanation.surface: Reporters crowd round, shielding the English upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists, but with 'closely' it means CRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its finest, most select members, an idiom for the best.

clue.text: Material used for construction in part of Turkey

definitions.meaning: interwoven rods and twigs, plastered with daub, used to build walls
the red fleshy fold of skin hanging from a turkey's throat

explanation.surface: A building material found in one region of the country Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Turkey look like the country; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the woven-stick building lattice, and the flap of skin on a bird's neck.

clue.text: Gold rush in the air for part of the year

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
a gust is a sudden rush of wind

explanation.surface: A gold rush seems to be in the air at a certain time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush in the air' reads as a feeling of excitement; it is a blast of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth month is one portion of the calendar year.

clue.text: Rare item that might need picking up? That's not good

indicators.note: not good tells us to leave out the letter for good

parts.words: item that might need picking up
parts.note: something lying on the floor might need to be picked up

explanation.surface: Something dropped on the floor needs picking up, which is a bad thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G from THING ON THE GROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce or hard to find is described by this idiom as rare.

clue.text: Car tax which was paid after one had to the end of the road

definitions.text: tax which was paid after one had to the end of the road

parts.note: an estate is a British car with a long rear load space, a station wagon
a duty is a tax on goods

explanation.surface: Motoring tax that was only settled after the driver reached the road's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to the end of the road' is a euphemism for dying; an ESTATE car is a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the former British name for death duty, a levy on a dead person's assets.

clue.text: Form of declaration with article in parcel one has ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A customs declaration form arrives with an item inside a parcel someone has ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like buying by mail; it signals that PARCEL plus AN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking or expressing things, an idiom or manner of declaring.

clue.text: Write warning note about hot sensations

indicators.note: the letters wrap about the one for hot, which sits inside them

parts.note: to pen is to write
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an omen is a warning sign
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone writes a warning about hot feelings or sensations.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes in after the P of PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon can be a sensation, something remarkable that creates a stir.

clue.text: A little light dressing on top of gherkins

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it
the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds

explanation.surface: A light salad dressing poured over pickled gherkins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' looks like salad dressing, but it is a wound dressing, LINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A glint is a tiny flash or gleam, a brief little shine.

clue.text: Chance getting a less than perfect mark

parts.note: to bet is to chance or risk something

explanation.surface: A student's prospects of scoring something below full marks.
explanation.definitionFit: In marking, beta is a second-class grade, good but below alpha.

clue.text: Takes advantage of one trying to sell alcohol

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
a tout pesters people to buy, as with tickets

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a person who is hawking booze.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweet dark beer brewed with lactose, an example of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Propose to thicken hard underlay for mats perhaps

parts.note: to table a motion is to propose it for debate
to clot is to thicken, as blood does
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A suggestion to stiffen a firm underlay beneath floor mats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mats' suggests floor mats; here they are table mats laid over the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Table mats are set on top of the fabric covering a dining table, so it lies under them.

clue.text: A twine woven net is constricting

parts.note: twine is string

indicators.note: woven suggests strands interlaced, so the letters of net are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A net woven from twine is tight and constricting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' turns NET into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringent substance draws tissue together, contracting or tightening it.

clue.text: The first day of grouse-shooting is so very enjoyable

definitions.meaning: the ... Twelfth is 12 August, when the British grouse-shooting season opens

explanation.surface: A shooting enthusiast says the opening day of the grouse season is a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, opens grouse-shooting in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense names the season's opening day by its nickname; the other means splendid or delightful.

clue.text: Boss has mainly to spend time learning

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to study is to spend time learning

explanation.surface: The employer mostly has to devote time to training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like an employer; here it is a raised knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob, and a stud is a similar decorative knob.

clue.text: A show of peers reviewing the matter of East Lothian

indicators.note: reviewing a matter means going over it again, so the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords hold an inquiry into East Lothian affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: East Lothian is a Scottish county. 'peers' are members of the House of Lords, who form the chorus of this Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: Iolanthe, or The Peer and the Peri, is a comic opera mocking the House of Lords.

clue.text: Bottom may have been raised on such a machine

definitions.text: Bottom may have been raised on such a machine

parts.words: Bottom may have been raised on such a machine
parts.note: Nick Bottom in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream is a weaver, so he might have grown up working at a weaving frame

explanation.surface: Someone's backside may have been lifted by some contraption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A weaver works at this frame, so a weaver like Bottom could be raised on one.

clue.text: Minerals from space? Time to stop

parts.note: a comet is a body coming from space
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: A question about space rocks, then a call that it is time to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to rest is a phrase meaning to stop moving or settle.

clue.text: Artificial gems, large and pale in colour

parts.note: paste is glass used to make imitation jewels
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: Fake jewels, big and with a washed-out hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastel shades are soft, light, delicate tints.

clue.text: Country — pre-eminent one involved in drug crop

indicators.note: being involved in something puts these letters inside the crop

parts.note: coca is the plant grown for cocaine
star means leading or outstanding
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A leading figure is caught up in growing a drug crop in some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: This Central American republic lies between Nicaragua and Panama, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Friend back in time to hold me

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other inside it

parts.note: ago means in the past
mi, or me, is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A pal wishes to go back in time to embrace the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' gives MI, the sol-fa note sometimes spelt 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a pal, used in English too.

clue.text: River that's dry by the end of June

indicators.note: by means beside, so the letter sits next to the first piece

parts.note: to air washing is to dry it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A riverbed that has dried up by late June.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aire flows through Leeds, so it is an example of a river.

clue.text: Stagger with small barrel

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: Someone lurches about holding a little keg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' reads as reel; here it means amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or shock them, the same as stun.

clue.text: Conspicuous old colour used in heraldry

parts.note: vert is the heraldic term for green

explanation.surface: An old shade that stands out on a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, so noticeable.

clue.text: Company expect an investment opportunity

parts.note: a unit is a body of soldiers, like a company
to trust that something will happen is to expect it

explanation.surface: A firm anticipates a chance to invest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' reads as a firm; it is a military company, a UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit trust is a pooled fund in which investors buy units, an example of an investment.

clue.text: Crowd violently jostling sleuth

indicators.note: jostling means pushing about, so the letters of sleuth are shoved into a new order

explanation.surface: A mob roughly pushes and shoves a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: To hustle someone is to push or jostle them roughly, to crowd them.

clue.text: God present in surrounding as before

parts.note: to pose a question is to present it

indicators.note: the word in surrounds the letters for ditto

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning as before

explanation.surface: A deity is present, surrounded as he was previously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' is ditto, abbreviated to two letters, a convention from lists and tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea.
